title: Anthropic Evaluation and Error Triage
summary: Turn a Claude workflow into measurable tests, preserve privacy-safe request evidence, classify provider failures, enforce total-attempt limits, and release or recover through explicit gates.
prerequisites: Access to application telemetry without secrets
Node.js 22 and PowerShell 7 for the offline exercise

sections.title: Define success before tuning
paragraphs: Write task-specific, measurable success criteria before changing a prompt, model, or application. Include representative cases, boundary cases, negative cases, and high-severity regressions. Use automated checks for schemas, required fields, calculations, citations, and prohibited outputs. Use calibrated judgment only where deterministic checks are insufficient. Reserve a holdout set for final comparison rather than tuning. These practices follow Anthropic's evaluation guidance: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests.

Record the workflow version, model configuration, dataset version, grader, thresholds, and results. Compare baseline and candidate across quality, safety, latency, cost, and operational slices. An overall average is not a sufficient release gate. Inspect severe slices and worst cases separately. If the grader or dataset changes, establish and label a new baseline rather than presenting the result as a clean comparison.

code.label: Evaluation record template
code.code:
Workflow/version: [name / commit]
Model/configuration: [configured model / parameters]
Dataset: [version / tuning split / holdout]
Grader: [automated checks / calibrated judgment]
Thresholds: [quality / safety / latency / cost]
Baseline versus candidate: [overall and slice metrics]
Worst case and blocking regressions: [filled evidence]
Decision: [PROMOTE | HOLD | REVERT]
Approver and timestamp: [owner / UTC timestamp]

sections.title: Classify the failure before acting
paragraphs: Separate local input failures, request validation failures, authentication failures, billing failures, permission failures, rate limits, spend caps, provider failures, overload, timeouts, streamed errors, application-validation failures, and uncertain downstream side effects. Record status, provider error type, request identifier, timestamp, configured model, total attempt number, latency, and a privacy-safe input fingerprint. Do not place API keys, authorization headers, prompts, completions, personal data, or payment data in ordinary diagnostics.

Anthropic documents HTTP 400 for invalid requests, including configured organization or workspace spend limits; 401 for authentication; 402 for billing; 403 for permission; 413 for oversized requests; 429 for rate or acceleration limits and also tier or monthly spend caps; 500 for API errors; 504 for timeouts; and 529 for overload. A spend-cap 429 lacks Retry-After and requires access restoration rather than blind retry. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors.

sections.title: Worked incident: classify, bound, and recover
paragraphs: This filled incident is synthetic and is not evidence from a live Anthropic account. At 12:00 UTC, an operation receives a retryable 429 on its initial provider attempt. The configured SDK policy makes two transient retries, so attempts 2 and 3 exhaust the application cap of three total provider attempts. The operator stops instead of adding an outer retry. A separate 429 has no Retry-After and account evidence identifies a monthly spend cap. The application assigns the synthetic normalized category SPEND_CAP, records the request identifier, stops automatic retries, and routes access restoration to the account owner. SPEND_CAP is an application category, not a claimed Anthropic wire error.type value.

Recovery evidence is also synthetic: the account owner records access restoration, the operator runs one approved probe under a fresh three-attempt budget, and the probe succeeds on its initial attempt. The redacted post-recovery record contains the timestamp, request identifier, application version, status, and attempt count. Automatic traffic resumes only after the probe, retry-budget review, and unresolved-side-effect count all pass. A 401, 402, or 403 instead requires credential, billing, or authorization repair. A 400 or 413 requires request correction. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors.

12:00:02 attempt 2/3: status 429, SDK retry 1
12:00:06 attempt 3/3: status 429, SDK retry 2

sections.title: Read severe slices, not only the average
paragraphs: This report is an illustrative synthetic evaluation, not an Anthropic benchmark or live-product result. The baseline passes 940 of 1,000 overall cases, while the candidate passes 942. The candidate therefore rises from 94.0% to 94.2%. However, the safety-refusal slice falls from 49 of 50 to 41 of 50, or 98.0% to 82.0%. The payment-confirmation slice falls from 97 of 100 to 76 of 100, or 97.0% to 76.0%. These severe regressions are hidden by the overall average.

The predeclared gate requires overall quality not to fall, every safety-critical slice to reach at least 95%, and no critical slice to regress by more than 2 percentage points. The candidate fails two blocking conditions, so the decision is HOLD_AND_REVERT. Preserve the dataset, holdout, grader version, report, and failed candidate. Restore the last verified workflow version and rerun the unchanged evaluation to produce post-rollback evidence.

sections.title: Bound retries, protect diagnostics, and reconcile uncertainty
paragraphs: Use an explicit transient allowlist and one total-attempt cap. Count the initial provider call and every SDK attempt in that cap. Anthropic documents that its SDKs retry transient errors twice by default. Therefore, an initial call plus two SDK retries consumes a three-attempt application budget. Do not add an outer loop that creates a fourth attempt. Eligible 429 rate or acceleration limits, 500, 504, and 529 may receive bounded backoff and jitter. Authentication, billing, permission, invalid-request, oversized-request, and spend-cap failures require correction or restored access instead of unchanged retries. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors.

An SSE error can arrive after HTTP 200, so a successful initial status does not prove the stream completed. Preserve the request-id header or error-body request_id for tracing, but omit sensitive bodies. If a timeout or stream interruption leaves a possible charge, message, order, or record update uncertain, mark the outcome UNKNOWN. Query the authoritative downstream system using a transaction or idempotency identifier. Retry only after reconciliation proves the operation was not applied or confirms that repeating it is safe. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors.

code.label: Provider-specific decision table
code.code:
Local missing or unknown fixture input: 0 provider attempts; reject locally
400 invalid_request or 413 oversized request: 1 attempt consumed; fix request
401 authentication: 1 attempt consumed; repair credentials
402 billing: 1 attempt consumed; restore billing
403 permission: 1 attempt consumed; repair authorization
429 rate or acceleration limit: bounded retry within total cap
429 tier or monthly spend cap: stop; restore access; no blind retry
500 api_error, 504 timeout, 529 overload: bounded retry within total cap
SSE error after HTTP 200: classify the stream event as a failed provider attempt
Unknown possible side effect: reconcile authoritative state before retry
Diagnostic bodies and secrets: do not log

sections.title: Offline exercise: replay provider attempts and repair one policy
paragraphs: This exercise uses deterministic fixtures and makes no network request. It models provider events, including initial and SDK-originated attempts, a transient recovery, exhausted overload, an SSE error after HTTP 200, authorization and billing stops, a synthetic spend-cap category, request errors, and unknown-side-effect reconciliation. It does not prove model quality, provider availability, pricing, latency, or actual account behavior.

The deliberately flawed starter really replays and counts fixture events, but its single decision area treats every error as retryable and ignores reconciliation. Only the unchanged success case passes initially. Repair that policy without editing fixtures or tests. The fixed independent suite runs all eight fixture cases plus missing-input and unknown-input checks. Node.js 22 supports ES modules, file-relative import.meta.url handling, promise-based file access, and child_process execution used here: https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html and https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html.

code.label: Exercise contract
code.code:
Runtime: Node.js 22
Command: node .\student.mjs <case-name>
Stdout: exactly one compact JSON object for a known case
Exit 0: known case handled, including a deliberate stop
Exit 1: missing input, unknown case, or unreadable fixture
Maximum provider attempts: 3 total, including initial and SDK attempts
Local command validation: 0 provider attempts
Fixtures and test.mjs: fixed independent evaluation artifacts; do not edit
Network and package installation: not used

sections.title: Create the exercise in a new directory
paragraphs: Run this PowerShell 7 script from the parent directory in one PowerShell session. It refuses an existing TRAINING-TRIAGE path before creating anything and contains no removal, overwrite, or cleanup command. It finishes inside the new exercise directory, so later commands must run from the current directory without another Set-Location. The script uses documented PowerShell commands: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/new-item, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/test-path, and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/set-content.

sections.title: Run and interpret the authentic baseline failure
paragraphs: From the current exercise directory, run the fixed suite before editing student.mjs. The exact baseline is RESULT 1/8 with exit code 1. The valid case passes. The 400, synthetic spend cap, 402, 403, three-event overload, and changed 413 cases fail because the starter labels them retryable. The rate case also fails: it reaches success in three counted provider events, but it omits the required reconciled:true evidence after the unknown-side-effect timeout. Both command-validation checks pass with exit code 1 and consume no provider attempts.

The 400 and 413 fixtures each contain an initial provider event, so their expected attempts value is 1. Zero attempts is reserved for local validation, demonstrated by missing and unknown command input. The baseline count follows directly from the starter and expected objects. It is deterministic expected output, not a claim that a live Anthropic call was executed.

code.label: Baseline command and exact expected summary
code.code:
node --version
node .\test.mjs
$baselineExit = $LASTEXITCODE
Write-Host "baseline exit code: $baselineExit"
# Exact fixture result: RESULT 1/8
# Exact test process exit code: 1
# Exact command checks:
# CHECK missing-input PASS exit=1
# CHECK unknown-input PASS exit=1

sections.title: Repair the bounded decision area
paragraphs: Edit only student.mjs. Replace the generic error continuation with status-aware decisions equivalent to the exercise contract. Stop after 400 or 413 and report validation. Stop after 401, 402, or 403 with the corresponding recovery action. Test normalizedCategory for the fixture's synthetic spend_cap category before treating another 429 as retryable. Allow only 429 rate limits, 500, 504, and 529 to advance within the three-event cap. Treat an sse_error using its provider status even though its httpStatus is 200.

Before advancing past an event whose sideEffect is unknown, inspect its reconciliation value. Continue only when it is not_applied, and include reconciled:true if a later provider attempt succeeds. Keep attempts incremented once per provider event, regardless of whether the event is initial or SDK-originated. Do not add an outer retry, hardcode fixture names, edit fixtures, edit test.mjs, copy reference.mjs over student.mjs, call a network, or install a package. The changed 413 fixture ensures the validation rule is based on input fields rather than the original invalid case name.

code.label: Repair checklist
code.code:
[ ] Preserve missing-input and unknown-input exit code 1
[ ] Increment attempts for every provider event, including HTTP 400 and 413
[ ] Cap initial plus SDK-originated provider events at 3 total
[ ] Stop authentication, billing, permission, validation, and spend-cap cases
[ ] Retry only the transient allowlist within the remaining budget
[ ] Interpret an SSE error after HTTP 200 from its streamed provider status
[ ] Reconcile an unknown possible side effect before another provider event
[ ] Attach reconciled:true to the later successful result
[ ] Base decisions on event fields, not fixture names
[ ] Leave fixtures and test.mjs unchanged

sections.title: Verify every positive, negative, recovery, and changed case
paragraphs: Run the suite from the current exercise directory. It launches student.mjs as a separate process for every case, parses complete JSON output, checks exit codes, and gathers all outcomes instead of stopping at the first failure. The unchanged positive case is valid. Negative cases include invalid, spend-cap, billing, permission, overload exhaustion, and the changed oversized request. The rate case exercises transient recovery, all three provider attempts, and reconciliation before its final success.

A correct repair prints PASS for all eight fixture cases, passes both local invalid-input checks, ends with RESULT 8/8, and exits 0. The exact expected objects below are the comparison values used by test.mjs. Attempt counts include the initial provider event and SDK-originated events. No random delay or clock is involved.

sections.title: Compare with the separate reference answer
paragraphs: Use reference.mjs only after attempting the repair. It is separate from student.mjs and is not installed as the starter. The reference demonstrates classification order, actual event replay, a shared three-attempt boundary, an SSE error event after HTTP 200, and reconciliation before retry. Its spend_cap value is explicitly a synthetic normalized application category attached to the fixture. It is not presented as an Anthropic wire error.type string.

The reference is still an offline teaching implementation. It omits real waiting, jitter, concurrent rate coordination, secrets management, provider SDK syntax, persistence, and a real downstream reconciliation query. Passing it or the learner suite establishes only that the deterministic application policy matches the fixtures.

code.label: Run the separate reference without replacing the learner file
code.code:
node .\reference.mjs valid
node .\reference.mjs rate
node .\reference.mjs spend-cap
node .\reference.mjs overload
node .\reference.mjs changed
# Expected outputs are the corresponding exact objects in the test section.
# Do not copy reference.mjs over student.mjs.

sections.title: Separate fixture replay from optional real-product validation
paragraphs: Deterministic fixture replay is not real API execution and is not evidence of Claude quality, Anthropic availability, pricing, latency, or a live account's error behavior. A separately approved real-product workflow would identify the exact configured model and application version, use managed credentials without exposing them in source or logs, capture request identifiers safely, test stream completion when streaming is enabled, and evaluate a versioned dataset and holdout. This module requires no secret and no network connection.

Before production use, verify the dated provider and SDK behavior selected by the product. Include internal SDK attempts in the application total, collect redacted per-attempt evidence, and test access-restoration and rollback procedures. Never infer model prices, model versions, or SDK call syntax from this exercise. If a real operation could have changed downstream state, retain the same transaction or idempotency identifier and reconcile the authoritative system before retrying.

code.label: Optional real-product evidence requirements
code.code:
LIVE EVIDENCE MUST IDENTIFY:
- dated provider and SDK documentation used
- exact application and configured model version
- approved credential handling and redaction controls
- redacted request identifiers, timestamps, statuses, and observed error types
- total provider attempts, including SDK attempts
- stream completion or post-HTTP-200 stream error evidence
- dataset, holdout, grader, thresholds, and severe-slice results
- downstream reconciliation evidence where side effects were possible
- rollback target and post-recovery verification

Offline fixture output must not be labeled as live evidence.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: A complete decision package contains the versioned evaluation report, holdout result, severe-slice metrics, independently reproducible operational test, redacted diagnostic record, retry-budget review, privacy review, and side-effect status. The synthetic candidate in this module is HOLD_AND_REVERT because its safety and payment slices fail predeclared blocking gates despite a higher overall average. Restore the last verified workflow version and rerun the unchanged evaluation before considering the rollback successful.

For an operational incident, stop when the shared total-attempt budget is exhausted. Escalate persistent provider failures with request identifiers and a redacted timeline. Restore credentials, billing, permission, or spend access before a new approved attempt when those categories apply. Close the incident only after a post-recovery probe succeeds, attempt accounting is within policy, error signals are healthy under the organization's declared threshold, and every possible downstream side effect is reconciled or explicitly remains open.

sections.title: Primary sources
paragraphs: Anthropic's API error documentation supports the status categories, distinction between rate limits and spend caps, absence of Retry-After for spend-cap 429 responses, request identifiers, errors during SSE after HTTP 200, and the documented default of two SDK retries for transient errors. Anthropic's evaluation documentation supports task-specific criteria, boundary cases, automated checks, calibrated judgment, and reserved evaluation data. Node.js and Microsoft documentation support the offline runtime and setup commands. All listed sources were reported checked on 2026-09-20; no browsing during drafting is claimed.
